findings.headline: The global easing cycle is under way, which is the backdrop against which Egypt normalises a 19.50% policy rate rather than the cause of it
findings.source_name: US Federal Reserve policy history as carried in the house rate schedule
findings.model_impact: Sets the direction, not the level, of the cost-of-debt path that the discount-rate glide inherits its shape from.

findings.headline: Cement is an energy-conversion business: solid fuel and electricity dominate cash cost, so the fuel bill is the single most important cost driver in the build
findings.source_name: Global Cement / International Cement Review industry coverage
findings.model_impact: Fuel is modelled explicitly as thermal energy per tonne of clinker times a blended fuel price, rather than buried in an assumed margin.

findings.headline: The EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism raises the landed cost of Egyptian cement in Europe; a low-carbon producer earns a relative premium estimated at about EUR 5.4 per tonne on European sales
findings.source_name: Industry coverage of Egyptian producers' CBAM positioning
findings.model_impact: Sets the export price path DOWN in dollar terms for the industry generally while giving this producer a smaller decline than a high-clinker peer would suffer; carried in the export price driver, not as a separate revenue leg.

findings.headline: Cement is not traded at distance — bulk freight caps the economic export radius, so global demand reaches an Egyptian producer only through the Mediterranean and East African basin and never through a world price
findings.source_name: Global Cement, Egypt country coverage
findings.model_impact: Justifies modelling a domestic price and an export price separately rather than applying one international benchmark.

findings.headline: The Central Bank of Egypt held the main operation rate at 19.50% (overnight deposit 19.00%, lending 20.00%) at its April and May 2026 meetings; headline urban inflation eased for a third month to 14.3% in June 2026, and the CBE expects it to accelerate through Q3-2026 on base effects before declining toward target
findings.source_name: Central Bank of Egypt policy decisions and Monetary Policy Report Q1-2026; CAPMAS CPI release
findings.model_impact: Sets the explicit-window risk-free anchor and the shape of the cost-of-debt path. The TERMINAL risk-free rate is norm-built from the CBE's own published medium-term inflation target plus a standard emerging-market real-rate convention — never a historical average and never reverse-engineered from a price.

findings.headline: Egypt's five-year credit default swap traded around 335 basis points in mid-2026, far tighter than the 2024 crisis peak
findings.source_name: Sovereign CDS quotations as carried by market data services; Damodaran country risk file, January 2026 edition, CDS column
findings.model_impact: The sovereign default spread is NETTED OUT of the local-currency risk-free rate before a country equity risk premium is added, so Egypt's default risk is charged once rather than twice.

findings.headline: The pound has been broadly stable around EGP 50.3-51.0 per US dollar through July and early August 2026
findings.source_name: Egyptian bank exchange-rate surveys reported by Amwal Al Ghad and Arab Finance
findings.model_impact: Sets the level of the currency path that converts the dollar-priced fuel bill and the dollar-priced export price into pounds. The two legs partly offset, which is why the path is carried as one driver rather than two.

findings.headline: Phased energy-subsidy reform continues to raise the domestic industrial energy bill independently of the global fuel price
findings.source_name: Egyptian cement industry market coverage on energy reform, currency volatility and raw-material management
findings.model_impact: Applies a local cost-inflation index to the pound-denominated cost lines, which is what prevents the margin from being held flat at the FY2025 peak.

findings.headline: Egypt's statutory corporate income tax rate is 22.5%
findings.source_name: Egyptian Tax Authority statutory rate
findings.model_impact: Floor for the tax rate used in the after-tax operating profit line; the rate actually applied is the effective rate implied by the company's own disclosed profit, which is higher.

findings.headline: Egypt abolished the cement production-quota system in May 2025 and capped exports at 30% of a producer's output; prices stabilised near USD 81 per tonne after the change
findings.source_name: Egyptian Competition Authority and Industrial Development Authority decisions as reported by Enterprise and Global Cement
findings.model_impact: The unlock that lets utilisation rise in the forecast, and simultaneously the reason the price path is set BELOW inflation: the same decision that frees volume also removes the mechanism that was supporting price.

findings.headline: With quotas gone, producers are studying the revival of seven to nine dormant production lines, potentially adding 12.6 million tonnes from the second half of 2026 — about 23% of domestic consumption
findings.source_name: Global Cement, Egypt update; Enterprise industry coverage
findings.model_impact: The single most important reason the realised-price path grows more slowly than inflation across the forecast, and the reason the asset lens is a ceiling rather than a floor.

findings.headline: Domestic consumption grew 13-14% to roughly 54 million tonnes in 2025 and cement sales rose 10.4% to 44.7Mt in FY2024/25; Portland prices ran 80-85% above the 2024 average during 2025 and are expected to settle near EGP 3,600 per tonne in 2026, with demand growth forecasts for 2026 spanning 1% to 8%
findings.source_name: Enterprise industry review of Egyptian cement 2025; Arab Finance building-materials indicators
findings.model_impact: Anchors both the FY2025 realised-price reconciliation and the deliberately conservative forward price path.

findings.headline: Egyptian nameplate capacity is about 76 million tonnes against roughly 54 million tonnes of domestic consumption and about 65 million tonnes of production
findings.source_name: Global Cement, Egypt country update
findings.model_impact: Fixes sector utilisation near 70%, which is the cross-check on this producer's own utilisation path and the reason no capacity expansion is modelled.

findings.headline: Egyptian cement and clinker exports were about 18.5 million tonnes in 2025, with finished-cement exports up sharply and clinker exports down
findings.source_name: Global Cement export coverage
findings.model_impact: Supports a higher realised export price per tonne than a clinker-weighted mix would give, carried inside the export price driver.

findings.headline: Dry preheater/precalciner kilns run at 3.2-3.6 GJ per tonne of clinker and 90-110 kWh per tonne of cement; replacement cost for grey-cement capacity sits in the USD 120-150 per annual tonne band and fixed cash cost in the USD 10-20 band
findings.source_name: Standard cement engineering and industry cost benchmarks
findings.model_impact: Every physical coefficient in the unit cost stack, and the replacement-cost anchor behind the asset lens and the terminal return on capital.

findings.headline: The listed Egyptian cement comparator set is thin and its published multiples are internally inconsistent: for one peer a quoted price/earnings ratio cannot be reconciled with the market capitalisation printed beside it
findings.source_name: Aggregated peer data cross-checked against reported profit and market capitalisation
findings.model_impact: The relative lens is struck on a RECOMPUTED peer multiple, and its weight is held down because the anchor is weak.

findings.headline: A cement producer with a clinker capacity of 4.2 million tonnes a year that can produce 5 million tonnes a year of cement, on two lines in Suez governorate
findings.source_name: Audited FY2025 statements note 1
findings.model_impact: Nameplate capacity, the base of the volume build, the denominator of the enterprise-value-per-tonne lens and the base of the fixed-cost line.

findings.headline: Net sales EGP 4.67bn (2022), 6.04bn (2023), 8.729bn (2024) and 12.447bn (2025, +42.6%); attributable profit EGP 358.98mn, 697.49mn, 1.160bn and 3.599bn; earnings per share EGP 3.02 (2024) and 9.49 (2025)
findings.source_name: Audited consolidated financial statements FY2023-FY2025, Deloitte (Wafik, Ramy & Partners), signed 25 February 2026
findings.model_impact: The disclosed history the whole model closes against, and the base year of the forecast.

findings.headline: Full-year 2025 operating income of EGP 4,595.82mn and a fourth-quarter EBITDA of EGP 1,393.01mn on fourth-quarter sales of EGP 3,645.60mn; trailing gross margin 40.77%
findings.source_name: Audited consolidated financial statements FY2025 — statement of profit or loss, and notes 5 and 6
findings.model_impact: The disclosed operating-profit anchor the bottom-up cost stack is calibrated to, and one of the three legs of the depreciation triangulation.

findings.headline: Total assets about EGP 8,783.72mn, total equity about EGP 4,642.73mn, total debt about EGP 1,035.19mn and cash about EGP 3,459.39mn on the latest reported balance sheet — a NET CASH position of roughly EGP 2.42bn
findings.source_name: Audited consolidated statement of financial position at 31 December 2025 and notes 19, 20, 21, 24 and 25
findings.model_impact: The enterprise-to-equity bridge, the capital-structure weights in the cost of capital, and the treasury-income line. Carried with an explicit caution: a separate aggregation prints total liabilities of EGP 2,894.13mn, which does not close against the same total-asset and equity pair, so the liabilities figure is DERIVED on the sheet and the disagreement is disclosed rather than averaged away.

findings.headline: First-quarter 2026 net sales EGP 2.995bn (from 2.554bn) and attributable profit EGP 943.068mn (from 590.347mn), +59.7% year on year, earnings per share EGP 2.50
findings.source_name: Reviewed condensed consolidated interim financial statements, three months to 31 March 2026, Deloitte, 25 May 2026
findings.model_impact: The reality check on the first forecast year: revenue growth has decelerated to +17.3% while profit growth remains strong, which is precisely the price-flat, margin-holding pattern the forecast assumes.

findings.headline: Cash dividends of EGP 1.10bn for 2024 (EGP 2.94 per share) and EGP 2.0bn for 2025 (EGP 5.34 per share), a payout of about 56% of attributable profit
findings.source_name: Audited FY2025 statements note 28 (general assembly resolution of 2 December 2025) and the Q1-2026 dividends-payable balance
findings.model_impact: Sets the forecast payout ratio and, through it, the cash roll-forward on the balance sheet. Also the sharpest cross-check on the share count: both distributions divide to the same count to within 0.2%.

findings.headline: Aridos Jativa, a Spanish company, owns 60% of the capital. The group also consolidates Andalus Concrete (99.99%), ACC Management and Trading (99%), Evolve for Investment and Project Management — the alternative-fuel arm — and Egypt Green for environmental services, both 99.99%. The company holds 1% of its own capital in treasury, acquired during 2025 under a board approval of 21 July 2025
findings.source_name: Audited FY2025 statements notes 1, 21 and 24
findings.model_impact: Context for the minority-position risk paragraph. No control premium or discount is applied anywhere in the valuation.

findings.headline: The company is Egypt's alternative-fuel leader — refuse-derived fuel and biomass substitution, a 7.2 MWh solar station commissioned in 2019, baghouse filters and hydrogen injection in 2024, targeting a 120,000-tonne annual emissions reduction — and is advancing supplementary cementitious materials, calcined-clay clinker and a CEM III product with 50% slag
findings.source_name: Company sustainability disclosure and industry coverage
findings.model_impact: The one genuinely company-specific cost lever in the build: the alternative-fuel substitution rate enters the fuel cost line directly, and the falling clinker factor enters the volume conversion. This is why the cost stack is not a sector average.

findings.headline: Closing price EGP 59.00 on 6 August 2026 (open 58.40, high 59.90, low 58.25) on 374.87mn shares — a market capitalisation of about EGP 22.1bn
findings.source_name: The supplied EGX daily series; share count corroborated by both dividend distributions
findings.model_impact: The anchor for every versus-spot comparison, the equity weight in the cost of capital, and the per-share conversion of every lens.

findings.headline: The supplied series runs 2,957 sessions from 18 May 2014 to 6 August 2026 with no placeholder rows, no unadjusted corporate action and a largest single-session move of 18.2% against the exchange's 20% daily limit; the share closes unchanged on 12.2% of sessions against an Egyptian library median of 9.0%
findings.source_name: House data-quality screen over the supplied series
findings.model_impact: Clears the price history for use in the probabilistic price map and in the beta regression, and quantifies the thin-trading bias the beta section has to answer.

drivers.justification: Built from nameplate cement capacity of about 5.0Mt times a kiln utilisation path, cross-checked two ways: against the disclosed share of Egyptian nominal capacity (about 6% of 76Mt = 4.6Mt) and against sector utilisation of roughly 70%. Quota abolition is the unlock that lets utilisation rise.

Domestic and export prices are carried separately. The FY2025 domestic price is the level the DISCLOSED revenue implies given the volume build and the export split, so the build ties back to the printed top line rather than asserting a price.

Thermal energy per tonne of clinker times a blended fuel price, where the blend is the company's own alternative-fuel substitution rate applied between a fossil and a refuse-derived fuel price. This is the company-specific lever and it is modelled as one, not folded into a margin.

An OUTPUT of the physical cost stack, not an input. It glides down from the FY2025 peak on two named, dated mechanisms — 12.6Mt of dormant capacity restarting from 2H-2026, and phased energy-subsidy reform — and is calibrated so the FY2025 reconstruction reproduces the disclosed operating profit.

No depreciation line is separately disclosed in any retrievable source. It is TRIANGULATED on the sheet by three independent methods — a fourth-quarter EBITDA-margin closure, a peer per-tonne anchor, and a net-property-base estimate times a composite rate — and averaged there rather than asserted.

No capital-expenditure guidance is obtainable. Capex is set at the ECONOMIC maintenance level in dollars per tonne of capacity rather than at book depreciation, because a historic-cost asset base in a currency that has devalued several times understates what it actually costs to keep the plant running. This is deliberately conservative and is stated as such.

drivers.driver: Cost of debt and the discount-rate glide
drivers.justification: The company is NET CASH, so the cost of debt carries almost no weight in the blended rate; the glide SHAPE is inherited from the cost-of-debt path implied by the central bank's own easing calendar rather than invented separately.

Norm-built from the central bank's own published medium-term inflation target plus a standard emerging-market real-rate convention. Never a historical average and never reverse-engineered from a target price.

Modelled as a yield on the modelled cash balance. No interest-income line is separately retrievable, so it cannot be built bottom-up. It is excluded from free cash flow to the firm entirely and handled in the equity bridge, so it cannot be double-counted.

Held at the 5% house default for an established emerging-market industrial once currency turbulence has passed, sensitised 3-7%, and reconciled against the return on capital that would have to fund it.

invariant_errors: COVERAGE: INDUSTRY / 'technology substitution' unclosed — needs a finding or a dated negative search
COVERAGE: COMPANY / 'one-off base-resetting transactions' unclosed — needs a finding or a dated negative search
invariant_warnings: FS DEPTH: 2 distinct fiscal years ['FY2024', 'FY2025'] — target is 4; below target but above the floor

uncovered.technology substitution: This study holds a COMPANY-ring finding on alternative fuels — refuse-derived and biomass substituting for imported coal in ARCC's own kilns — and that is a real technology-substitution observation. It is not an INDUSTRY-ring finding, and no search of the Egyptian industry's substitution rate is recorded. The category stays open rather than being closed by moving the finding's ring.
uncovered.one-off base-resetting transactions: No search for a one-off base-resetting transaction is recorded. Whether there is nothing to find or nothing was looked for cannot be told from this register, which is exactly the state the coverage invariant is meant to make visible.

qc_line: 26 findings across four rings, 6 blocking-or-driver-unlock in the country and industry rings and 6 in the company ring; every forecast driver names the findings it rests on and declares whether it is built bottom-up or top-down. Built through the shared register so its eight invariants run; 2 still fire and each is named.
